Triage first-touch grade (concentrated batch; triage seat, session `session_01NYoiJGd1MxXdcvM4EGAMrS`): promoted to `pm:queue`, type **Bug** — `columns="[object Object]"` / `props="[object Object]"` in shipped DOM is wrong output even while layout survives it, and every catalog grid example renders with it today.

Direction endorsed: whitelist the DOM passthrough in `grid.tsx` (#3291's discipline — allow legal HTML/`data-*`/`aria-*` only), rather than enumerating known schema keys to strip; the enumeration re-rots. Also answer the card's own side-question in the PR: why React's unknown-lowercase-attribute warning never turned a test red (that answer decides whether a warning-as-error pin is worth adding so the class stays closed). Size/model suggestion: S, sonnet.

Clause-②: no — stopping schema keys from leaking into DOM attributes narrows what reaches the DOM, it does not change what the schema accepts or widen the public surface. ⚠️ Flips if the fix requires changing which keys `GridSchema` **declares**; that is spec-side, and Fable 5 is exhausted for this seat, so stop and report rather than dropping tier.
Serial constraints cleared: none — `packages/components/**` has no in-flight claim in this lane and no round-1/2 PR touched this file. Note for awareness, not a conflict: `packages/components` is a large shared package, so keep the diff to this one renderer.

Located on `origin/main` this round: the leak is in `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/grid.tsx` (sole match for the `mdColumns`/`mdcolumns` vocabulary).

⚠️ **The observable is the rendered DOM, not the React tree.** `columns="[object Object]"` and `mdcolumns="2"` are invalid HTML attributes that React emitted because the schema object was spread onto a host element. A test asserting "the grid renders" is green against the broken code. Assert that the offending attributes are **absent from the rendered element**, and keep a positive control proving the attributes that *should* survive (whatever the renderer legitimately forwards) still do — otherwise a fix that strips everything passes just as well.

Standing instruction for this round: **read this card's full comment thread, not just the body.**

## PM · review of PR #5573 — the side-question answer is worth more than the fix

Triage asked why React's unknown-attribute warning never turned a test red, and said the answer decides whether a warning-as-error pin is worth adding. You did not guess; you measured **four independent reasons**, and together they close the question in the opposite direction from the one a quick look would suggest.

1. **React only warns for camelCase keys.** On `origin/main` the canary leaked **eight** attributes and produced **three** `console.error` calls — `mdColumns`, `smColumns`, `colorVariant`. The all-lowercase ones (`columns`, `gap`, `name`, `props`, `zzcanary`) warn **not at all**, because React passes unknown lowercase attributes through by design and stringifies object values silently. **Both attributes this card's title names are in the silent set.**
2. **Vitest 4's reporter defaults to `silent: 'passed-only'`**, so console output from a passing test is discarded outright.
3. **React latches the warning per prop name per module instance** — it fires only on the *first* render carrying a given key.
4. …and reason 3 is not theory. **Your own case 3 was vacuously green against the broken renderer**, because cases 1 and 1b render first and consume the latch for every key they carry. **Your reverse verification caught it** — green on code that leaked ten attributes — and you fixed it with a canary key (`zzCanaryCamel`) authored nowhere else in the file.

That fourth point is the one I want on the record. A test that passes against the broken code is the exact failure this repo keeps paying for, and you found it in your own work, from the ablation, rather than shipping it. Then you wrote **"Do not let this case's green be read as coverage"** into the file so the next reader cannot misread it either.

The conclusion follows and I accept it: **a warning-as-error pin is not worth adding here.** It would be blind to the majority of this very defect. Case 1 closes the class because it reads the DOM instead of the console.

### The shape follows triage's ruling, and follows it for the stated reason

`toDomProps` from `@object-ui/core` — the whitelist #3291 established in `packages/fields` and #4425 phase 2 promoted to the SDUI widget contract. **Reused, not re-derived.** And case 1 asserts the *whole attribute set* against what the contract declares DOM-safe rather than naming today's bad keys, with the reasoning spelled out: naming `columns`/`gap`/`mdcolumns` would pass against a renderer that strips those four and leaks the rest, would re-rot on the next schema addition, and **could never reach the open tail** — `zzcanary` and the flattened `props` container are author-supplied, so no finite list of schema keys names them. That is the "enumeration re-rots" ruling understood rather than obeyed.

**The positive control is load-bearing and you said why:** a renderer that stripped everything satisfies the absence assertions on its own, so case 2 pins the computed grid classes, the merged authored `className`, `id`, `role`, both open families (including the designer's `data-obj-id`/`data-obj-type`, which now arrive through the `data-*` prefix rule instead of being hand-forwarded), the forwarded `style`, and the children.

`style` forwarded **by name** rather than reopened in the shared whitelist is the right call, with the right reason: the shared set is deliberately element-agnostic, and a container's designer sizing channel is element-specific (#4435's route).

### Status

Path surface (`get_files`): 3 files — `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/grid.tsx`, one new test, one changeset. Scope held to the single renderer as claimed; no governed surface → ordinary ready → merge-queue path.

CI on #5573 has not converged. No verdict and no enqueue until the gate jobs read `completed: success` by name.

- **Recommendation: do not add a warning-as-error pin here.** It can only catch the camelCase half, would read as "class closed" while `columns="[object Object]"` passed untouched, and is order- and reporter-sensitive. The DOM-reading sweep (#5574) is the guard that actually closes the class.

Read by name: `Test (shard 1/4)` `(2/4)` `(3/4)` `(4/4)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Control Byte Scan`, all three changeset gates, both doc type checks, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Build Docs`, `Live E2E` → every one `completed: success`. **19 success / 3 skipped / 0 failures / 0 in progress.**

Substantive review is in the comment above. Two things from your terminal report that arrived after it and belong on the record:

**Case 2 staying green under ablation is the point, and you read it correctly** — *"case 2 (the POSITIVE CONTROL) stayed GREEN against the broken code, which is the point — it proves it is a control, not the detector."* A positive control that went red would have been a second detector, not a control.

**#5574 reframes this card's real scope, and it is the more valuable output.** The #3291/#4425 DOM-leak sweep gate **targets only four plugin packages and never reaches the `packages/components` renderers** — which is *why* `ui:grid` leaked unobserved — and `flex.tsx`, `stack.tsx`, `container.tsx`, `text.tsx` still carry the identical bare spread. Recording them as "candidates to measure, not asserted as defects" is the right register: you did not touch them, and you did not claim them as bugs you had not measured.

That also lands the recommendation where it belongs. The card asked whether a warning-as-error pin was worth adding; the answer is no, and the pin that *would* close the class is extending this DOM-reading sweep to the components renderers. #5574 carries it, open and unassigned for triage.
